collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older and another adult)

collection.description: A villager admits sleeping through every wonder of the night for years: defend their sleep, or ask to hear it all.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the fire, people are remembering the great night of the shooting stars, years ago, when the sky was full of them. (friend) describes it beautifully. Everyone who was there joins in. (subject) listens politely, then admits, "I slept through it." Everyone stares. "And the night of the glowing sea. And the night the whales came into the bay. I slept through all of them."

choices.label: Ask Them to Tell It Properly

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks them to describe every one of the nights (subject.he/she) missed, properly, with all the details. They do. It takes all evening. (subject) lies back and listens with (subject.his/her) eyes closed, imagining it all. "That's lovely," (subject.he/she) says at the end. "And I didn't even have to get up." Somebody throws a nut at (subject.him/her).

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "I'm a very good sleeper," (subject) says, with dignity. "It's my gift." (friend) laughs so hard (friend.he/she) chokes. (subject) explains that (subject.he/she) has missed every wonder of the night for twenty years and does not regret a single moment of rest. Everyone agrees, laughing, that next time something wonderful happens, they will NOT wake (subject). (subject) says thank you.
